alpha_client_native_layout_revision.rationale: A 16-byte shift of the start of the protected segment can expand its trailing padding by one linker alignment unit, without allocating another page or increasing the final file or initialized RELRO payload. The mathematical benefit is elimination of a false simple-root certificate. The bounded exception is disallowed if any PT_LOAD page range changes or any new mapped page is required.
alpha_client_native_layout_revision.guard: Measure on a fresh linked build at the same source path. For each PT_LOAD retain the same page addresses and permissions. Require unchanged initialized PT_GNU_RELRO payload, no increase in file bytes, and the same protected pages. All other ELF metrics, WASM, runtime, heap, stack, certainty and trace gates apply.
alpha_client_native_layout_revision.history: The default cap was 6 bytes at 656 bytes of preceding padding. The first trial grew by 544 bytes and remains rejected. The separate paired-status trial grew by one 16-byte linker unit and failed that original gate. Fixed padding was 1,424 bytes. Previous positive charge was zero. The cumulative effective cap remains 28 bytes. Rejected trials consume no budget.

quadratic_alpha_proof_classification.benefit: Return honest proof statuses for unknown or approximately compared zero values under both public policies.
quadratic_alpha_proof_classification.policy: existing_artifacts with the one Rust 1.99 native NOBITS exception at alpha_client_native_layout_revision. Its new allowance is used only after the independent same-path rebuild. Original failure measurements are archived.
quadratic_alpha_proof_classification.evidence: docs/evidence/2026-11-19-interval-solver-orientation: matched-client-sizes.json, alpha-matched-registered-sizes.json, alpha-deploy-sizes.json, layout-evidence.json and full section reports; no firmware artifact links the proof API.

rational_fractional_power_ingress.scope: Generated rational endpoints in the fractional power consumer. Compare final linked public clients on Linux and bare Wasm plus owner release tests and cost drivers on Linux and WASI. The optional native replay coordinator uses its existing premium over the corresponding ordinary image. The reduced 1.88 feature lane builds an empty harness. Firmware selects integer/fixed backends. No rational power code reaches those linked firmware images.
rational_fractional_power_ingress.caps: Public linked file, code and nonoverlapping function bytes: 4096 B and 1% incremental, 8192 B and 2% cumulative. Also limit bare Wasm to 1024 B incremental and native functions to 1024 B and 0.5%. Each 64 MiB tool slot retains 16 MiB. New test harness limited to 4 MiB. Existing ordinary, coordinator and legacy accounts retain their own limits and prior positive charges.
rational_fractional_power_ingress.details: records/accounted.json contains per-image fixed, preceding, candidate, prior charge, step, cumulative charge and remaining allowances. Native earlier sources recompiled at the same path. coordinator-account.json carries each coordinator premium. No savings credited against growth.

machine_travel_qualification.scope: First size registration for these unshipped Linux conformance tools. Each target shares its fixed baseline across future charges. The campaign process limit is 1536 MiB per worker. It does not describe firmware memory or flash.

generated_square_root_admission.scope: Rational and dyadic square-root kernel, generated-source budget admission and two release regression suites. Eight linked native/bare Wasm client images and eight native/WASI regression images. The optional allocation observer is built separately. Firmware uses integer/fixed.
generated_square_root_admission.allowances: Native client file and code 4096 B/1% per change, 8192 B/2% cumulatively. Native functions also cap at 1024 B/0.5% per change. Bare Wasm 1024 B/5% per change and 4096 B/10% cumulatively. Both ingress suites 32768 B/2% per change and 65536 B/4% cumulatively, also subject to their 4 MiB file limit. All host slots 64 MiB with 16 MiB reserved. Existing cost and test accounts retain their individual limits.
generated_square_root_admission.linked_owner_consumers: The fixed, preceding and retained builds and SHA-256 sums cover 20 indirect native tests and benchmarks on each compiler. Also measured sqrt_cost, fractional_power_cost, and two previously registered narrow-feature cost drivers. Maximum positive indirect code step was 336 B, maximum function step 369 B. The fixed inverse_functions comparison separately links the same atanh oracle to the fixed library. Legacy narrow tangent and power link images retain 324 and 288 load pages. Their uninitialized RELRO padding grew 312 B and 1464 B. Power protects five pages after relinking, previously four. Its initialized RELRO payload fell 24 B.
generated_square_root_admission.details: Archive members size-accounted.json and caps.txt contain individual charges, predecessor values and headroom. layout-pages.json separates file-backed payload, page protection and zero-fill alignment. All linked public clients use fewer mapped native pages or a smaller bare Wasm image.

csgrs_bevy_executor_release_client_budge.benefit: Admit the upstream executor lifetime repair used by the optional Bevy desktop renderer and its scoped task consumer. The named artifact links actual packaged csgrs and Bevy on x86_64 Linux.
csgrs_bevy_executor_release_client_budge.scope: The matched optimized 0.23.0 public Bevy release client on Rust 1.95.0 and 1.99.0, in a 64 MiB host-tool slot with 16 MiB reserved.
csgrs_bevy_executor_release_client_budge.original_caps: File and text 4096 bytes and 1% per change, 8192 bytes and 2% cumulative. Functions additionally restricted to 1024 bytes and 0.5% per change.
csgrs_bevy_executor_release_client_budge.first_screen: On 1.95.0 the upstream 1.14.1 patch grew file, text and function union by 50376, 6320 and 6177 bytes. Rebuilding the 1.14.0 client with the observer targets present reproduced the original SHA-256. Earlier unaffected 1.13.3 grew the same metrics by 50288, 6304 and 6177 bytes. On 1.99.0 the patched client grew by 1536, 4608 and 4788 bytes. Historical screens remain recorded.
csgrs_bevy_executor_release_client_budge.rationale: Sixteen file pages and four executable pages per step accommodate a compatible memory-safety repair in a 16–18 MB desktop executable. The smaller of the byte and percentage caps applies separately to each metric. Prior positive charges remain due at the fixed program baseline, independently on each compiler. The exact consumer results, matched memory, confirmed final linked measurements and headroom must pass before retention.

csgrs_bevy_executor_release_qualificatio.benefit: Use the unyanked patch that repairs the upstream desktop executor lifetime.
csgrs_bevy_executor_release_qualificatio.caps: See csgrs_bevy_executor_release_client_budget. Three Linux GUI slots each use the same step and cumulative file, text and function caps, with a 128 MiB slot and 32 MiB reserved. Wasm requires byte identity on this step.
csgrs_bevy_executor_release_qualificatio.method: The archive records absolute totals, caps, remaining step and cumulative allowances and separate checksums for every final image. Cargo uses the executor only in the native normal dependency graphs of the three demos.

proposal_midpoints_and_rk4_subnormal_bou.benefit: Round both primitive proposal midpoints once under round-to-nearest with gradual underflow and preserve tiny initial ranges and stage values in RK4.
proposal_midpoints_and_rk4_subnormal_bou.scope: Final Rust release images at matched checkout and client paths. The unversioned images use Rust 1.95, stable is 1.99. Measured direct midpoint, radius and materialized midpoint/radius clients, downstream workloads, augmented tests and a simulated Thumb hard-float consumer. Per-image SHA-256 and auxiliary native read-only data inventory are in final-size.json in the archive.
proposal_midpoints_and_rk4_subnormal_bou.accounting: Both absolute and percentage caps apply separately to each metric. Carry forward the larger of the observed positive fixed-to-preceding delta and the published prior charge for the same radius or test client. File includes metadata for native and Wasm. Embedded flash uses occupied loadable extent including gaps. Native named_text deduplicates symbol aliases and Wasm counts emitted function bodies.

trigonometric_endpoint_conformance.benefit: Detect false whole images and incorrect domain coverage for unresolved right endpoints. Verify exact tight bounds and exhaustion/retry at dyadic output boundaries with nondegenerate inputs.
trigonometric_endpoint_conformance.scope: Rust 1.95 release all-feature Hyperinterval integration test executables, one matched checkout and target path per compiler target. Host qualification slot 64 MiB, required free 16 MiB per image.
trigonometric_endpoint_conformance.limits: Both 2% and the absolute cap apply at each step and cumulatively. The file cap is 32 KiB. Executable code and defined-function bytes each have a 16 KiB cap. Remaining is after both limits. Native charges carry forward the larger of the published earlier charge and observed positive fixed-to-preceding growth.
trigonometric_endpoint_conformance.wasm_control: The fixed historical manifest refused cross-compilation. Its isolated fixture adds the WASI-only GMP force-cross development feature and lock edge from the current build. The fixed Rust source is unchanged. Hashes and build-metadata diff are archived.

univariate_krawczyk_row_certainty.benefit: Row classification and its division fallback use certified comparisons on univariate quadratic boxes. The public point-box and strict-contraction controls return honest proof outcomes under both policies.
univariate_krawczyk_row_certainty.original_caps: Defaults for native allocated sections were 4096 bytes and 1% incremental, 16384 bytes and 2% cumulative, with separate function and file limits. All original dispositions are retained in caps.txt and the trial accounts.
univariate_krawczyk_row_certainty.native_padding_revision: Rust 1.95 Linux SHT_NOBITS .relro_padding only. For each full-report and allocator-usable client, at most 256 bytes incremental and 512 bytes cumulative (6.25% and 12.5% of one 4096-byte page). No additional pages in any PT_LOAD or GNU_RELRO, larger file, or changed permissions. The ordinary lifetime target reserves zero new padding. Its cumulative ceiling of 3208 bytes (78.3203125% of one link page) carries the entire pre-existing same-path fixed-to-control debit. Each retained segment must fit the fixed page count. The cumulative allowance is fully spent. For each of the registered certification benchmark, smoke suite, native trace observer and stress lifetime instrument, at most 256 and 4096 bytes (6.25% and 100% of one link page) with no growth in total load pages, initialized RELRO payload, executable code or final file. Retain all prior debits, including historical increases between fixed and previous. Record each segment separately. Firmware receives no allowance.
univariate_krawczyk_row_certainty.qualification_test_revision: For the new acceptance cases in krawczyk_univariate_algebraic alone, each of the four final native and WASI qualification images has a 49152-byte and 2% step cap, and a 65536-byte and 3% cumulative cap for file, code and defined-function size. The introductory 442615f77 image anchors each budget. The initial 16 KiB proposal and the separate test/combined library pilots are preserved. Shared fixture extraction left multivariate code and function sizes unchanged.
univariate_krawczyk_row_certainty.note: final-account.json contains effective byte/percentage caps, allocation flags and positive-only charges by target and metric. The 42 registered release targets have a separate feature-qualified accounting in all-budget-review.json. Nine upstream Hyperlattice interval targets had different features from the registry. A pre-existing positive fixed-to-control debit on a metric is preserved even when the current change allocates zero bytes there.
univariate_krawczyk_row_certainty.retained_fuzz_scope: The fixed 2026-11-15 driver lacks two replay workloads introduced at 8fa4de4a9. Preserve the measured change between the two suites and the raw historical comparison. Compile the original benchmark sources against fixed, preceding and repaired libraries, and the expanded suite separately against its introduction, preceding and repaired libraries. The standard incremental and cumulative caps hold for each completed suite. No new charge for code or functions in either comparison.

saturated_coefficient_diagnostic.benefit: A simultaneous 32-bit ceiling in a coefficient denial now reports a justified lower bound. The executable suite also checks both individually representable counts across the 512 nested triples.
saturated_coefficient_diagnostic.program_budget: Carry the historical c9f1f9ac5 solver and legacy accounts, the 063cb703d nested suite and the c73863d18 produced-denominator test file charge. The 282fec460 matched release is the preceding revision. The new standalone formatted-error clients use their first matched 282fec460 images as their workload baseline.
saturated_coefficient_diagnostic.caps: Legacy file, executable code and defined-function bytes: 4096 bytes and 1% incremental, 8192 bytes and 2% cumulative (earlier target-specific caps and exhausted accounts remain binding). New fixture assertions: 16384 bytes and 1% incremental, 32768 bytes and 2% for the new assertion series, retaining historical full image charges and the 16 MiB ceiling. Standalone clients: 4096 bytes and 1% incremental, 8192 bytes and 2% cumulative, at most 16 MiB file.
saturated_coefficient_diagnostic.raw: size-review.json contains all 44 per-image comparable accounts. public-images.json contains both bare modules and both native libraries. The 1.95 native owner benchmark has identical loaded bytes outside its build ID. No firmware links Hypersolve in the measured program.

schedule_equivalence_decoder_compatibili.scope: Phase 11 schedule-equivalence test and fuzz byte decoder. Rust 1.99 strict all-target Clippy now passes. Production code is unchanged.
schedule_equivalence_decoder_compatibili.program_baseline: Keep the previously registered d8eb6fa0c harness accounts. No positive change in final file, executable code or defined function bytes on any measured target. Earlier charges stay reserved.
schedule_equivalence_decoder_compatibili.limits: 64 MiB for each complete executable, 16 MiB reserved. No size exception spent.

wasi_path_and_interface_tests_2026_11_19.scope: Hosted single-thread wasm32-wasip1 release test commands. Hyperpath development-only binaries have their first measured baseline here. Interface is compared with the preceding 196-test image on precisely the same dependency revisions. The additions exercise existing firmware actor tests. All native Hyperpath controls match byte for byte.
wasi_path_and_interface_tests_2026_11_19.units: bytes; code is the code section payload, bodies is the sum of defined function body payloads

hyperpath_two_hosted_relro_padding_limit.target: Rust 1.95 x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu release, all Hyperpath features
hyperpath_two_hosted_relro_padding_limit.scope: Only the .relro_padding SHT_NOBITS section of the certified_schedule example and schedule_equivalence integration suite. The linker reserves this space through the end of a page protected after relocation. The preceding section-size percentage gave different allowances for the same page capacity. Every file-backed, code, memory, performance and dispatch account keeps its existing limits.
hyperpath_two_hosted_relro_padding_limit.required_condition: Each PT_LOAD and GNU_RELRO segment keeps its page count and permissions against both the original and preceding release. The examples and tests each retain a 16 MiB reserve in the registered 64 MiB hosted command slot.
hyperpath_two_hosted_relro_padding_limit.original_disposition: The original incremental 1% section allowance rejected +24 on 1,648 and +40 on 2,760. No other artifact receives this revision.

hyperpath_certified_tangent_joins.units: Bytes in file, executable .text or WASI code payload, and union of named text ranges or sum of WASI function bodies, in that order.
hyperpath_certified_tangent_joins.caps: Hosted slot 64 MiB with 16 MiB reserved per target. Native file, .text and allocated sections 4096 B/1% incremental, 16384 B/2% cumulative. Native named text 1024 B/0.5% incremental and 4096 B/1% cumulative. WASI file/code/bodies 1024 B/5% incremental and 4096 B/10% cumulative. See hyperpath_two_hosted_relro_padding_limits for the two named ELF reservations.
hyperpath_certified_tangent_joins.accounting: Same-location before and after for each delta. Cumulative totals charge positive growth for each metric independently. Native historic deltas and all nonzero section charges with both remaining limits are in cumulative.json in the evidence archive. WASI uses the same-source reconstruction of the originally registered guest release. New test commands establish separate initial measurements.
hyperpath_certified_tangent_joins.native_interface_symbols: Release strips native symbols. .text measures native machine code; zero named-range bytes is the symbol table observation.

mixed_degree_affine_box_review.admission: Reviewed trials only. Primary debit is zero.
mixed_degree_affine_box_review.scope: 88 existing release library/test, example and benchmark commands per toolchain and architecture, plus one new integration command per trial. Three complete four-way comparisons and a separate four-command measurement for alternatives.
mixed_degree_affine_box_review.raw: strict-comparison.json, family-comparison.json and sparse-comparison.json give per-target sizes, positive and negative changes and slot headroom. Raw paired ELF and WASI metrics include every allocated ELF section, function range union or aggregate WASI body size. Original registered accounts are preserved.
